newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: South Korea November gas oil exports seen limited.
newsitem.headline: South Korea November gas oil exports seen limited.

text.p: South Korean spot gas oil exports for loading in November are seen largely unchanged from October at between four and six cargoes, industry sources said on Wednesday.
The amount of gas oil that is available for export is much less than the 10 cargoes that were sold in September due to increased domestic sales, traders said.
One major refiner has acquried around 1.5 million barrels of 0.1-percent sulphur diesel from two other local refineries for deliveries in November and December.
Traders said the large purchase was partly to tide the company over until the start up of a new refinery unit in November and to compensate for reduced term purchases this winter.
"November supplies could be reduced further if the winter turned cold," traders warned.

South Korean refiners have reduced October availabilities as they have built stocks ahead of the coming winter. But they may still raise stocks further if the country faces unseasonally cold weather in coming months, traders said.
Traders said South Korean refiners would prefer to export the higher valued 0.1 percent sulphur gas oil, rather than the 0.5 percent product that is consumed in China.
But the sale of 0.1 percent gas oil depends on Japanese demand which right now is subdued due to rising stock levels and refinery runs.
The 0.5 percent cargoes were sold in October at about 35 cents premium to Singapore spot quotes while a 0.1 percent cargo was sold at about $1.00 premium, both on a fob basis.

South Korean gas oil exports in November are also dependent on how well Yukong Ltd's, the country's largest refiner, new crude unit operates and how quickly the company restarts its other crude unit which was shut down for maintenance on Tuesday.

The 200,000-bpd new crude unit was successfully started up over the weekend after a slight delay. It is currently operating at 90 percent capacity and company officials said they hope to have it running at 100 percent by Friday.
Yukong's 265,000-bpd other CDU is scheduled to restart on November 14.
